Read the transitions of a fit or an inference result

Source: R/filter-transitions.R, R/transitions-inference.R
transitions.Rd

transitions() returns the transitions of a lag sequential analysis as a table, one row per ordered pair of states, from a fit and from every result built on a fit. The transitions are the substance of the analysis: for each ordered pair of states, how often the second follows the first at the chosen lag, how often independence would predict, and whether the difference is larger than chance. A positive adjusted residual marks an over-represented transition, one the process prefers; a negative residual marks an avoided one. Yule's Q, kappa and lift express the same association on bounded or ratio scales.

On a fit from lsa(), a grouped fit or a multi-lag fit from lsa_lags(), it returns the estimated statistics of each transition. On the result of bootstrap_lsa(), certainty_lsa(), stability_lsa(), permute_lsa(), compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa(), it returns that method's per-transition quantities. The arguments narrow and order the table: significant = TRUE keeps the transitions the method flags (significant for a fit, a permutation test or a group comparison; stable under resampling for the bootstrap, certainty and stability results), direction keeps over- or under-represented transitions, min_count drops rare ones, and sort puts the strongest first.

Use nodes(), tests() and initial() for the other tables of a fit, and lag_profile() to follow one transition across lags.

Usage

transitions(fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
transitions(
  fit,
  significant = FALSE,
  direction = c("any", "over", "under"),
  min_count = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  sort = c("none", "strength", "count", "prob"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
transitions(
  fit,
  significant = FALSE,
  direction = c("any", "over", "under"),
  min_count = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  sort = c("none", "strength", "count", "prob"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_bootstrap'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_certainty'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_stability'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_permutation'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_comparison_pairwise'
transitions(fit, significant = FALSE, sort = c("none", "strength"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_lags'
transitions(
  fit,
  significant = FALSE,
  direction = c("any", "over", "under"),
  min_count = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  sort = c("none", "strength", "count", "prob"),
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit, a grouped fit, an lsa_lags result, or the result of bootstrap_lsa(), certainty_lsa(), stability_lsa(), permute_lsa(), compare_lsa() or bayes_compare_lsa().

...

Arguments passed to the method.

significant

Keep only the transitions the method flags as significant or stable (default FALSE).

direction

For fits only: "any" (default), "over" (significant with a positive residual) or "under" (significant with a negative residual). "over" and "under" imply significant = TRUE.

min_count

For fits only: keep transitions observed at least this many times. Default NULL (no filter).

alpha

For fits only: significance level. Default NULL uses the alpha of the fit.

sort

Row order: "none" (default, table order) or "strength" (largest absolute effect first: the adjusted residual for a fit, a bootstrap, certainty or permutation result; the stability proportion for stability_lsa(); the group difference for a comparison). Fits also accept "count" and "prob" (largest first).

Value

A data.frame with one row per transition. For a fit the columns are from, to, lag, count, expected, prob (row conditional, \(P(\text{to} \mid \text{from})\)), prob_col (column conditional, \(P(\text{from} \mid \text{to})\)), adj_res, p, yules_q, kappa, kappa_z, kappa_p, lift (observed over expected), sign ("over", "under" or "expected", comparing the count with the expected count) and significant; engines that compute further statistics append them (the two-cell engine adds odds_ratio, log_or and log_or_se). For an inference result the columns are from, to and that method's quantities, described on its help page; a pairwise comparison adds group_a and group_b. A grouped fit gains a leading group column, an lsa_lags result one row per transition and lag.

See also

lsa(), nodes(), tests(), initial(), transition_probabilities(), lag_profile()

fit <- lsa(engagement)
